elements.problem: Section header 'Treat the HIV positive patient in labour'. This red box is a treatment box, not a 'Give urgent attention' box, so it implies no priority evaluation or diagnosis.
Continue ART, take viral load, review at the postnatal visit: treatment and monitoring, no triage or diagnostic criterion.
Single-dose NVP plus TLD if not on ART: drug management.
Timing of the dose. 'Urgently if delivery is imminent' governs drug timing, not patient priority, so it is not a priority evaluation.
Start ART the next day (cross-reference to p126): management.
Infant prophylaxis by risk (cross-reference to p186): management of the baby, not adult triage.

Holds conditional criteria: aspirin indications (hypertension, diabetes, SLE, antiphospholipid syndrome, previous pre-eclampsia), 'If gestational hypertension' and 'If proteinuria/new symptoms, refer urgently'. All of them select treatment or referral for an already-diagnosed condition; there is no 'X likely' or 'consider X' and no red-box priority. The urgent referral in the gestational-hypertension follow-up is the closest thing to triage, but it is a management/referral step, and the triage belongs to the antenatal/hypertension pages (179).
